title: Bandmaster
raw_text:
8-420C. Military Occupational Specialty 420C--Bandmaster
    a. Licensing/certification requirements. None.
    b. Prerequisites. DA Circular 601 series.
    c. MOS 420C. MOS 420C is an accession MOS. The enlisted feeder MOSs is in MOS 42R.
    d. Associated SQI.
         (1) 0--No special qualifications.
         (2) 8--Instructor.
         (3) P--Parachutist.
         (4) T--Transition (personnel only).
         (5) Z--Research, Development, Test, and Evaluation Technician.
    e. Associated ASI.
         (1) 1J--Operational Electronic Warfare Operations (personnel only).
         (2) 1K--Tactical Electronic Warfare Operations (personnel only).
         (3) 1X--Black Belt in Lean Six Sigma (personnel only).
         (4) 1Y--Green Belt in Lean Six Sigma (personnel only).
         (5) 1Z--Master Black Belt in Lean Six Sigma (personnel only).
         (6) 2B--Air Assault (personnel only).
         (7) 3R--Force Management.
         (8) 5W--Jumpmaster (personnel only).
         (9) 6M--Mobilization and Demobilization Operations.
         (10) 6P--Master Fitness Trainer.
         (11) 6Q--Additional Duty Safety Officer (Reserve Component personnel only).
         (12) 6T--Military Auditor (Reserve Component personnel only).
         (13) 7Q--Training Development.
    f. Qualifications.
         (1) WO1/CW2 must--
               (a) Be a U.S. citizen. Qualify for a security eligibility of SECRET.
               (b) Complete the Army Music Warrant Officer Basic Course.
         (2) CW3 must--
               (a) Meet qualifications described in paragraph f (1).
               (b) Complete the Warrant Officer Advanced Course.
         (3) CW4 must--
               (a) Meet qualifications described in paragraph f (2).
               (b) Complete the Warrant Officer Staff Course (WOSC).
         (4) CW5 must--
               (a) Meet qualifications described in paragraph f (3).
               (b) Complete the Warrant Officer Senior Staff Course (WOSSC).
    g. Duties.
         (1) WO1/CW2--
               (a) Conduct or lead Army bands and Music Performance Teams (MPT) in support of
official military and civilian ceremonies and functions.
               (b) Select music appropriate for MPTs and their missions.
               (c) Direct rehearsals and performances to achieve desired musical effects, technical
knowledge, and talents of individual performers.
               (d) Participate in CONUS and OCONUS civilian and military community relations
functions representing the U.S. Army or the United States at the highest national and international
levels.
               (f) Provide subject matter expertise on military traditions, ceremonies, and music to
assigned command.
               (g) Supervise unit personnel in the execution of company level administrative duties.
         (2) CW3 performs duties described in paragraph g (1).
         (3) CW4:
               (a) Performs duties described in paragraph g (2).
               (b) Supervise junior WO (WO1/CW2) assigned as unit executive officer.
         (4) CW5 performs duties described in paragraph g (3).
               (a) Serve as Army Music Proponency Officer.
               (b) Serve as Army School of Music Assistant Director of Training.
    h. Physical demands category, grading and position titles.
         (1) Physical Demands Category (PDC) – Moderate (gold).
         (2) Table 8-420A-1. Physical requirements.
         (3) Physical demands rating for initial award of AOC. Adjutant General’s Corps Army
Music officers must possess the following qualifications:
              (a) A physical demands rating of moderate (gold).
              (b) A physical profile of 323222.
              (c) Qualifying scores. A minimum OPAT score of Standing Long Jump (LJ) – 0120
cm, Seated Power Throw (PT) – 0350 cm, Strength Deadlift (SD) – 0120 lbs., and Interval
Aerobic Run (IR) – 0036 shuttles in Physical Demand Category in “Moderate” (Gold).
         (4) The following grades are used to code positions into one of four definable skill levels:
W2 equals WO1/CW2; W3 equals CW3; W4 equals CW4; and W5 equals CW5. The grades are
listed in the following standards of grade tables:
              (a) Table 8-420C-2. Standards of grade TOE/MTOE.
              (b) Table 8-420C-3. Standards of grade TDA.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
